A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G2PT study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. The material supports a reliable comparison without identifiable completeness gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-generation, molecular optimization, property-prediction, scaling, and edge-ordering experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including G2PT benchmark scores, fine-tuning outcomes, scaling curves, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The tokenization, Transformer decoder, negative-log-likelihood training, RFT/SBS, PPO implementation, and prediction-head formula are retained. Algorithm 1 explicitly adds edge-list reversal, but v1 already specifies this in Section 3.1. The equation corrections and new MLP wording do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Planar, Tree, Lobster, SBM, QM9, MOSES, GuacaMol, the same eight MoleculeNet classification datasets, and QED/SA/GSK3β optimization tasks. No dataset, domain, or distinct testing scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GEEL comparisons on all four generic graph datasets. Table 4 adds GEEL and LigGPT on MOSES and GuacaMol. These extend the existing comparator sets; the QM9 and property-prediction comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged, including Appendix B and Tables 6–8. Section 5.7 changes 705M to 707M, matching Figure 3 in both versions; this resolves a documentation inconsistency rather than establishing a new model configuration.

E4.justification: The planar representation comparison, pre-training controls, model/data scaling analyses, and MOSES edge-ordering sensitivity analysis are retained with the same evidence. Appendix D's qualitative graph and molecule examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 5 reports the same means and standard deviations over three runs in both versions. No additional seed information, uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 4 add GEEL/LigGPT result entries while retaining existing scores. GEEL's new SBM clustering MMD of 0.003 beats G2PTbase's unchanged 0.0053, although Section 5.3 retains the old claim of 11 best scores out of 24. The remaining experimental results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a formal connection between sequence and graph likelihood through a KL/entropy lower-bound derivation and a conditional-KL gap, absent from v1. v2 also corrects the negative-log-likelihood expansion and revises the displayed RL KL expression, while removing some detailed conditional factorizations from the earlier Section 2.

C1.justification: The central contributions—efficient graph tokenization, autoregressive G2PT, downstream fine-tuning, and strong benchmark performance—remain. The introduction adds a stronger comparative claim that learning whole-graph representations is not feasible with diffusion-based generative models.

C2.justification: v2 adds arguments that additional sequences per graph can tighten the conditional-KL gap and that autoregressive generation makes the final-token representation informative for prediction. It also explicitly argues that modeling capacity outweighs losing permutation invariance. Existing empirical interpretations and the order-sensitivity limitation remain.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly states that code is released and supplies a repository address; v1 provides neither. v2 also reconciles the scaling-model size description with the existing 707M figure label. Appendix implementation details, hardware, and hyperparameter tables otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning around permutation-invariant versus sequential models and adjacency matrices versus edge lists, adding discussions such as GraphDF and DAGG. New Appendix C.3 situates G2PT among graph Transformers and explicitly contrasts its tokenization with Kim et al. (2022) and Gao et al. (2024), substantially expanding the related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work section, and substantial portions of the method and fine-tuning explanations are rewritten. Section 2's numbered mathematical review becomes a thematic literature discussion; Appendix C gains a subsection, and impact and acknowledgment sections are added. This exceeds localized copyediting.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 gain baseline rows, Table 1 changes labels and its final comparison column, and Table 3 relabels the proposed representation. Algorithm 1 is relocated and surrounding content reflows. The five figures and their underlying visual evidence are retained without a substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The added GEEL/LigGPT comparisons, fuller research positioning, clearer exposition, and code-access information provide a modest overall improvement. The core empirical evidence is unchanged. Benefits are tempered by the new derivation's inconsistent normalization between summed likelihoods and KL/entropy terms, and by the retained best-score count overlooking GEEL's superior SBM clustering result.
